chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: High-note trumpeters: Tommy Stevenson, Al Killian and Shad Collins
summary: He praises Tommy Stevenson's altissimo with Lunceford, Al Killian's range in Redman's band, and underrated Shad Collins.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Then, of course, I can go down to -- in the thirties I played with Al Killian Kahan in Don's band. Al Kahan was playing high notes before Maynard Ferguson or any of those guys. In fact, there was one trumpet player before him, even, Tommy Stevenson, that was with the original Jimmy Lunceford Lunceford band.
He used to play altissimo concert A-flats, which would be a trumpet B-flat.
They played 'Tiger Rag' and he used to hold that all the way through a whole chorus he'd hold that note.
And, of course, Tommy, he was a playboy and life got him and of course he died. Then came Al Killian Kahan. Al Kahan had a lip that was

unbelievable. I worked with him in Don Redman's band.
And, of course, Shad Collins. Shad Collins was, to me, an underrated trumpet player.
A very underrated trumpet player and a very good trumpet player and a good musician, a very good musician.
But the records speak for themselves if you hear the records --
